result.topic_en: Fragment 42 (attributed to J. A. Euler, with a note by Krafft) gives a descent criterion for deciding whether an equation $fxx+gyy=hzz$ is solvable, by repeatedly replacing $h$ with $\frac{h(pp+fg)}{qq}$ to reduce it to smaller numbers, worked on the example $7xx+113yy=114zz$.
result.transcription:
208 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Arithmetica.

42.
(J. A. Euler.)

Criterium ad dignoscendum, utrum hujusmodi aequatio $fxx+gyy=hzz$ sit possibilis, nec ne?

Si est possibilis, casu $h=a$, tunc etiam erit possibilis casu $h=\frac{a(pp+fg)}{qq}$: hic scilicet pro $p$ ejusmodi numerus sumi debet, ut $pp+fg$ divisorem habeat $a$, fuerit nempe $pp+fg=ab$ et sumto $q=a$ etiam casu $h=b$ erit possibilis. Tum vero pro $b$ eodem modo operatio instituatur, sicque continuo ad minores numeros pervenietur, donec tandem judicium fiat facile.

Exemplum. I. Sit $7xx+113yy=114zz$, quae aequatio an sit possibilis, quaeritur. Hic est $f=7$, $g=113$, et quaeritur an sit possibilis casu $h=114=2.3.19$? Statuatur ergo
$h=\frac{114(pp+791)}{qq}$ et sumto $p=3$ et $q=40$, prodit casus $h=\frac{114.800}{1600}=57$.

II. Nunc iterum fiet $h=\frac{57(pp+791)}{qq}$ et fiat $pp+791$ divisibile per 19, quod si fieri potest, dabitur casus quo $p<19$. Ut, ex. gr. $pp+12$ fiat divisibile per 19, debet esse $p=8$, unde $h=\frac{855}{3.19}=15$.

III. Quaestio ergo huc est reducta, an aequatio $7xx+113yy=15zz$ sit possibilis? quae hoc modo repraesentetur $15zz-7xx=113yy$, ubi $f=15$, $g=-7$, $fg=-105$ et $h=113$. Nunc fiat $h=\frac{113(pp-105)}{qq}$ et reddatur $pp-105$ divisibile per 113, quod fit sumendo $p=52$, tum autem fiat $h=\frac{113.2599}{\Box}=\frac{113.113.23}{\Box}$, ergo quadrato sublato fit $h=23$ et quaestio huc est reducta, an aequatio $15zz-7xx=23yy$ sit possibilis.

IV. Fiat ergo $h=\frac{23(pp-105)}{\Box}$ sitque $pp-13$ per 23 divisibile, sive $pp=23n+13$, quod fit si $n=1$ et $p=6$, ergo $h=\frac{-23.69}{\Box}=-3$. Habetur igitur haec aequatio
$15zz-7xx=-3yy$, sive $7xx-3yy=15zz$,
ubi $f=7$, $g=-3$ et $fg=-21$, $h=15$.

V. Fiat nunc $h=\frac{15(pp-21)}{\Box}$. Sumatur $p=4$, erit $h=\frac{-15.5}{\Box}=-3$, ergo aequatio $7xx-3yy=-3zz$, quod actu evenit si $x=0$ et $y=z$, atque hinc sequitur ipsam aequationem propositam esse possibilem.

Nota. Revera autem est possibilis: si enim capiatur $z=2$ et $y=1$, fit
$7xx+113=456$ sive $7xx=343$ et $xx=49=\Box$.
Ita semper aequatio si fuerit possibilis, ad talem formam reduci poterit $axx+byy=azz$, cui manifesto satisfit sumendo $y=0$ et $z=x$.

(Krafft.)

Judicium hoc reddi potest adhuc facilius hoc modo:
Cum sit $h=\frac{2.3.19(p^2+791)}{q^2}$, capiatur $p$ ita, ut $p^2+791$ divisibile fiat per $2.3.19$. Primo autem fit divisibile per 2, si $p=2n+1$; at vero per 3 fit divisibile, si $p=3n\mp1$. Utrumque igitur obtinetur, si $p=6n\mp1$. Restat, ut $p^2+791$ sit per 19 divisibile; quod fit, si $p^2$ per 19 divisum relinquat 7; sive debet esse $p^2=19n+7$, ergo $19n+7$ debet esse quadratum, quod fit, si $n=3$, eritque $p=8$. In genere ergo hoc fiet si $p=19n\mp8$, hoc est casibus $p=8$, $p=11$, $p=27$, $p=30$, $p=46$, $p=49$, $p=65$, etc. inter quos numeros reperitur statim 11, qui est formae $6n\mp1$. Sumatur ergo $p=11$, eritque $p^2+791=912=114.8$, ergo $h=\frac{114^2.8}{\Box}$ et sublatis quadratis $h=2$. Res ergo eo redit, an sit $7x^2+113y^2=2z^2$. Quia hic est $h=2$, sumatur iterum $h=\frac{2(p^2+791)}{q^2}$. Ponatur $p=7$, erit $h=\frac{2.840}{q^2}=105$. Si sumsissemus $p=3$, prodiisset

methods.what: Descent criterion: if $fx^2+gy^2=hz^2$ is solvable for $h=a$, it is solvable for $h=a(p^2+fg)/q^2$; choose $p$ with $a\mid p^2+fg=ab$, $q=a$, to pass to $h=b$, iterating to smaller numbers
methods.quote: Si est possibilis, casu $h=a$, tunc etiam erit possibilis casu $h=\frac{a(pp+fg)}{qq}$

methods.what: Worked reduction of $7x^2+113y^2=114z^2$ through $h=57,15,23,-3$ to a trivially solvable equation
methods.quote: ergo aequatio $7xx-3yy=-3zz$, quod actu evenit si $x=0$ et $y=z$, atque hinc sequitur ipsam aequationem propositam esse possibilem.

methods.what: Any solvable equation reduces to the form $ax^2+by^2=az^2$, solved by $y=0,z=x$
methods.quote: Ita semper aequatio si fuerit possibilis, ad talem formam reduci poterit $axx+byy=azz$, cui manifesto satisfit sumendo $y=0$ et $z=x$.

methods.what: Krafft's refinement: choose $p$ by congruence conditions so that $p^2+791$ is divisible by $2\cdot3\cdot19$ ($p=6n\mp1$, $p=19n\mp8$), giving $p=11$ and reducing to $h=2$
methods.quote: Sumatur ergo $p=11$, eritque $p^2+791=912=114.8$, ergo $h=\frac{114^2.8}{\Box}$ et sublatis quadratis $h=2$.

items.english: Thus an equation, if it is possible, can always be reduced to such a form $axx+byy=azz$.
